findings.title: Do not print cookie values
findings.evidence: request_value returns Option<String> containing the Cookie field. The code converts absent value to empty String then formats sent with String Debug; session=sensitive-value is emitted verbatim apart from string escaping.
findings.remedy: Report only whether a cookie field is present and/or jar count. Do not log the returned String, names or values.
findings.verification: Focused synthetic-cookie output assertion with a sentinel secret, absence/presence positives, followed by compile-check of cookies feature example at integration.

findings.title: Reject another origin before page I/O
findings.evidence: Url::join accepts absolute and // authority targets. The fetch factory installs sec-fetch-site same-origin for trustworthy origin and copies caller Referer; it does not compare target with page. No comparison exists in this example, so a foreign HTTPS URL is sent with misleading same-origin metadata after the first page request.
findings.remedy: Compare normalized page/fetch origins immediately after parsing/joining, before client creation or first send. Reject a foreign scheme, host or effective port. Keep legitimate relative and same-origin absolute targets.
findings.verification: Pure input controls for relative, absolute same origin, effective default port and foreign scheme/host/port/network-path negatives; prove the guard runs before client/I/O. Compile-check at integration.

findings.title: Keep query fields out of status diagnostics
findings.evidence: Both success println statements interpolate complete Url. A valid supplied ?token=sentinel remains in the printed URI. This is concrete accepted caller input copied to diagnostics, not a claim that userinfo/fragment is sent.
findings.remedy: Print operation plus status and optional origin only; omit path/query from diagnostics. Keep path/query in same-origin HTTP target and caller-owned Referer.
findings.verification: Pure diagnostic formatting assertion rejects query/path sentinel while keeping useful operation/status; ensure URL request/Referer bytes are otherwise unchanged.

findings.title: Point to the current template guide
findings.evidence: Module rustdoc names docs/guides/profiles.md for Apply a captured request template. That heading lives in docs/guides/request-templates.md at this commit.
findings.verification: Source pointer check and repository documentation checker at integration.

findings.title: Apply import and guard grouping standards
findings.evidence: Local use declarations follow module declarations; five independent target validation guards are packed without blank paragraphs. Attached standards prescribe imports before module declarations and visually separated guards. No runtime correctness defect inferred.
findings.remedy: Move local imports ahead of mod declarations and add blank paragraphs between independent target guards, without splitting domain owners or changing behavior.
findings.verification: Targeted rustfmt check plus diff review; no mirrored tests for paragraph-only edits.

qualifications: No credentials/fragment Referer exposure established: initial Client::get delegates to parse_absolute_uri, which rejects # and @. A credential/fragment page fails before send, success diagnostics and Referer construction; invalid fetch fails its own get before fetch send/println. The current example may already have performed page I/O for an invalid fetch.

The fetch template deliberately has a caller-owned Referer slot. Its expansion copies caller values without browser referrer-policy derivation. Same-origin path/query belongs to this caller input contract; no query-stripping remedy is proposed for the Referer. Cross-origin rejection is required by this example advertised task.

SSE and WebSocket intentionally expose potentially indefinite connected operations; this review does not invent a total example-lifetime promise. Additional CLI deadlines are a product choice, not an established defect.
Malformed Autobahn case outcomes are reported by the suite; exact case counts/nonempty reports/adapter exit are checked separately. No zero-observation green approval inferred.
